output.summary: Deterministic verdict: PASS, scoped to the single evaluated policy. The analysis reports run_validity VALID, analysis_coverage COMPLETE, and policy_verdict PASS for the overall-errors policy check (error_rate_ratio <= 0.01), with observed 0 errors out of 2623 overall samples. Overall latency percentiles are p50 11ms, p95 46ms, p99 77ms, max 904ms; the "home" transaction shows the same max 904ms with p99 96ms. All six transaction summaries (add product to cart, cart, checkout, home, product, reset cart) report error_count 0 with ~437-438 samples each, consistent with the overall sample_count 2623. Findings is empty, so no anomaly was flagged. This advisory treats the PASS as valid only for the sampled run and the error-rate metric: no latency, throughput, or per-transaction policies were evaluated, no timestamps or clock relationships are present, throughput_rps numerator/denominator semantics are undefined in the evidence, and the 904ms max-vs-p99 gap warrants a bounded follow-up check.

hypotheses.observation: Overall error_count is 0 and error_rate_ratio is 0/2623; policy check overall-errors (observed 0/2623, threshold 0.01) has status PASS, with run_validity VALID and policy_verdict PASS.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: The sampled JMeter run produced no failing requests as captured in the JTL/CSV, so the error-rate policy passed. This characterizes only the executed 2623 samples and does not prove failures cannot occur under different load, timing, or code paths.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Verify that the JTL/CSV ingest captured all samplers and response statuses without filtering or aborted samplers, and confirm the thread configuration and sampling interval that produced sample_count 2623.

hypotheses.observation: Overall max latency is 904ms while p99 is 77ms, and the 'home' transaction shows max 904ms with p99 96ms.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: A single sample or a short-lived tail spike (e.g., first-iteration warmup or transient resource contention in the 'home' transaction) could account for the 904ms maximum, but aggregate percentile summaries alone cannot identify when or why it occurred.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Pull the per-sample or per-time-bucket latency series for 'home' and overall, locate the sample(s) at or near 904ms, and inspect its timestamp and concurrent conditions.

hypotheses.observation: Each transaction summary reports approximately 437-438 samples with error_count 0, summing to the overall sample_count 2623.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: The script appears to execute each transaction a near-equal number of times, suggesting roughly 437 iterations per sampler; equal sample counts do not by themselves indicate load level, spare capacity, or stability.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Inspect the JMeter thread group (threads, ramp-up, loop count) and test duration in the run configuration to interpret the sample distribution and what load it represents.

hypotheses.observation: Overall throughput_rps is reported with numerator 2623000 and denominator 44986, but the semantic definition of these quantities is not stated in the evidence.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: The throughput figure may be derived from cumulative timing over an elapsed window, but without a defined unit and window any derived rate cannot be verified from this evidence alone.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Confirm in the producing analysis tooling what the numerator and denominator of throughput_rps represent (units, window, and derivation) before quoting a requests-per-second figure.

recommendations.action: Accept the PASS verdict for the overall error-rate policy as scoped to these 2623 sampled requests, and record that this analysis contains no latency, throughput, or per-transaction policy checks.
recommendations.rationale: The only policy_check evidence is overall-errors (error_rate_ratio <= 0.01) with observed 0/2623 and status PASS; a PASS on this metric is not evidence about any other metric or policy, and missing policies are not passes.

recommendations.action: Investigate the 904ms maximum latency observed overall and in the 'home' transaction before treating the aggregate latency percentiles as representative of behavior.
recommendations.rationale: Overall p95/p99 are 46/77ms and home p99 is 96ms, far below the 904ms max; the tail may be a rare event that aggregate percentile summaries do not characterize.

recommendations.action: Add per-interval latency and error time-series collection (or retain per-sample JTL rows) and verify clock alignment across collectors before forming any temporal or causal hypothesis.
recommendations.rationale: The evidence contains only aggregate summaries with no timestamps; without time-series data or verified clock relationships, no spike attribution, temporal ordering, or lead/lag hypothesis can be tested.

recommendations.action: Document the numerator/denominator semantics of throughput_rps (units and measurement window) and, if needed, capture wall-clock test start/end before reporting throughput.
recommendations.rationale: The raw numerator 2623000 and denominator 44986 in the overall summary are not self-describing; citing a rate requires a defined basis.

caveats: The policy verdict PASS applies only to the single policy check on the overall error_rate_ratio (threshold 0.01, observed 0/2623); the analysis contains no latency, throughput, or per-transaction policy checks, and their absence is not treated as a pass.

findings is empty and analysis_coverage is COMPLETE, but the supplied evidence is aggregate summaries only; absent findings and zero error counts do not prove stability, spare capacity, low load, or absence of problems.
sample_count 2623 (per-transaction ~437-438) covers only the executed run; error-free results do not generalize to other loads, durations, or code paths.
No timestamps or clock relationships appear in the evidence, so no temporal ordering, lead/lag, or causal timing hypothesis is supported without clock verification first.
No baseline or previous-run comparison is present, so no regression or improvement can be asserted.
throughput_rps numerator/denominator semantics are not defined in the referenced evidence, so any throughput claim requires a definition from the producing tooling.
Latency percentiles are the only latency representation available; the 904ms maximum cannot be located in time or attributed to any event from this evidence alone.

Error counts and throughput numerator/denominator are treated literally as reported (0/2623 and 2623000/44986 respectively); no error attribution to the JMeter run is inferred beyond what the summaries state.
